svg.title: Generic microlocal coefficients and isolated algebraic carriers
svg.desc: The exact real slice of the complex conormal model Y given by z1 equals zero, with h equal z1 plus t squared, fixes z1 at zero and its normal covector at one. In the remaining coordinates t and xi_t, the conormal is xi_t zero and graph dh is xi_t twice t. Their unique intersection is transverse. The actual microlocal stalk test inverts arbitrary denominators; comparison with vanishing cycles is used only at the weak complex constructible endpoints. A finite regular composition series gives an algebraic closed carrier, and analytic isolation plus faithful flatness gives its isolated point component. A common microsupport bound supplies the actual unbounded Ind regular point retract. Examples distinguish monodromy from coefficient complexes, ordinary cycles on a real halfplane from the microlocal test, and a doubled point scheme from its reduced carrier. Characteristic support equality remains separate.
svg.text: Generic microlocal coefficients and isolated carriers
Nonzero generic covector; smooth conic Lagrangian; constant projection rank.
1. An exact transverse conormal slice — MCM.1–MCM.12

graph: ξₜ=2t
C: ξₜ=0
Real slice of the complex cotangent chart.
Y={z₁=0}, h=z₁+t².
Fix z₁=0, ξ₁=1; plot (t,ξₜ).
C ∩ graph dh is one reduced point.
Φₕ(F)ₓ ≃ M ⊗ oₕ[−d] ≠ 0.
d=dim Y; oₕ is a degree-zero line.
This is an isomorphism of complexes.
2. Invert the actual denominators — MCM.3–MCM.9
F ≃ M_Y in the category localized at p.
The test Tₕ(A)=(μ_T A)ₚ is exact on arbitrary bounded sheaf objects.
A cone with microsupport avoiding p is sent to zero, so its arrow is inverted.
Compare Tₕ with Φₕ only at the two weak complex constructible endpoints.
An ordinary neighbourhood isomorphism or a monodromy isomorphism is not assumed.
3. Analytic isolation gives the algebraic point component — MCM.13–MCM.16
Regular finite composition factors j_!* E give the actual closed carrier Z.
Analytic density of each stratum: supp DR(B) = Z analytic.
Isolated point germ: I·H = m·H; faithful flatness contracts this to I=m.
Kill the finite maximal-ideal generators by one denominator: Dₛ = C.
Z = {x} ⊔ Z′, with Z′ closed and avoiding x.
Z is the reduced carrier; actual fibre-scheme nilpotents are retained.
4. The common support hypothesis yields the actual retract — MCM.17–MCM.19
Every coherent A in every HᵐE has SS(DR A) inside the same local C.
One h transverse to C isolates every bounded cycle carrier at x.
The isolated algebraic neighbourhoods may depend on A.
IAC point adjunctions give Φₕ(E) ≃ i_* i! Φₕ(E) ⊕ Q(E).
One bounded nonzero point coefficient injects into the full unbounded coefficient.
Operator characteristic support is a further comparison, not this premise.
5. Three explicit distinctions — MCM.20–MCM.26
Punctured-line sign system j_! L[1]: Φ_z coefficient C, monodromy −1.
Its point coefficient model has the same C and monodromy +1.
Real halfplane N=C_{a≥0}, p=db: Tₕ(N)=0 by horizontal pullback.
The actual nearby coefficient is product over all logarithmic strips.
Φₕ(N) = (product_Z C / diagonal C)[−1] ≠ 0.
Doubled point C[t]/t²: same isolated point set; tangent dimension one.
Its reduced carrier has local ring C and tangent zero.
Analytic isolated carriers do not establish a reduced cotangent fibre.
The real denominator cone is outside the weak complex endpoint comparison.
Exact proofs: §§3.302–3.311; MCM.1–MCM.26; Solutions3.EK,3.EL,3.EM.
Generic source coefficients are transferred through the microlocal stalk test.
SS(DR A) = Char(A) remains a separate cotangent-support assertion.
The common support premise in the actual Hecke application still requires proof.
Full-image regularity, nilpotent equality and special enhanced field generation remain separate.
